findings.title: Backup-code login can bypass password check
findings.body: In packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts password verification is guarded by `if (user.password && !credentials.totpCode)`. The new branch `if (user.twoFactorEnabled && credentials.backupCode)` takes precedence when a backupCode is supplied. An attacker who obtains a valid backup code can send both `totpCode: 'x'` (any non-empty value to make the password check false) and `backupCode: <valid>` and authorize() will skip verifyPassword entirely and log in on backup-code alone. Backup codes are meant as a second factor replacing TOTP, not as a replacement for the password. Consequence: leakage of a backup code (downloaded file, screenshot, copy) alone yields account takeover without the password.

findings.title: Backup code match is case/whitespace sensitive
findings.body: In packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts line 144 and apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts line 61 the code does `backupCodes.indexOf(credentials.backupCode.replaceAll("-", ""))`. It only strips dashes. Generated codes are lowercase hex from crypto.randomBytes().hex, displayed as XXXXX-XXXXX. User-typed uppercase, surrounding spaces, or other whitespace will not match and returns IncorrectBackupCode for a valid code. It also calls .replaceAll without verifying the value is a string, so a non-string payload throws. Consequence: legitimate backup codes are rejected on manual entry, locking out users who lost their authenticator.

findings.title: Backup codes stored reversibly instead of hashed
findings.body: In apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/setup.ts backup codes are persisted as `symmetricEncrypt(JSON.stringify(backupCodes))` and later decrypted for comparison in next-auth-options.ts and disable.ts. Unlike the TOTP secret which must be reversible, backup codes could be one-way hashed like passwords. With the current design anyone who reads the users table and obtains CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY recovers all 10 usable backup codes in plaintext. Consequence: larger blast radius on DB plus key disclosure; violates single-use credential best practice.

findings.title: Backup-code consume is non-atomic and reusable under race
findings.body: In packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts the backup-code flow does read-decrypt-indexOf then `backupCodes[index]=null` then a separate prisma.user.update to re-encrypt. Two concurrent authorize() calls with the same code can both read the same array, both find the same index, and both succeed before either write nulls it. Consequence: the exactly-once guarantee claimed in backup_code_instructions is violated; one backup code can be used twice.

findings.title: Throws instead of returning 500 on crypto failures
findings.body: In apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts missing encryption key, missing twoFactorSecret, and secret-length mismatch do `throw new Error(ErrorCode.InternalServerError)` inside a Next.js API handler instead of `return res.status(500).json(...)`. The same file also does unguarded `JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...))`. A throw escapes the handler, yields an unhandled 500 HTML response instead of the JSON error contract the UI expects, and can crash/log stack. Consequence: client cannot parse body.error, shows generic failure, and observability is degraded. This pattern is newly added for the backup-code path.

findings.title: No test for backup-code login or disable
findings.body: In apps/web/playwright/login.2fa.e2e.ts the PR adds only download/copy/close assertions for the backup-code screen and leaves `TODO: add more backup code tests, e.g. login + disabling 2fa with backup`. The new security-critical paths - login with backupCode in next-auth-options.ts including single-use invalidation, and disable with backupCode - have zero automated coverage. Consequence: regressions like reuse, password bypass, or normalization bugs will not be caught before merge.
